title: Austin's 1908 Challenges: Street Funding & Dog Control
summary:
• **Dog Muzzling Ordinance Passes** – City Council approved an ordinance requiring all dogs running at large to be muzzled, but limited the enforcement to June through October each year.

• **Street Projects Face Financial Hurdles** – Mayor Maddox vetoed a proposal to open Fourth Street in Hyde Park, citing the city's lack of funds and the petitioners' failure to contribute promised money toward the project.

• **Public Space Designated for Farmers' Wagons** – The Council designated a city block on East 5th Street between Neches and Trinity Streets as a marketplace where farmers could sell produce from wagons, clearing the area for public commerce.

• **Infrastructure Investments Approved** – The city authorized spending on street repairs ($500 extra labor), Barton's Creek road improvements ($200), Congress Avenue paving ($1,000), and a retaining wall project ($2,200).

• **Dog Catcher Elected & City Services Funded** – Los Evans was elected dog catcher, and the Council approved numerous appropriations for street cleaning, cemetery maintenance, and city hall improvements (hitching posts and railings for $175).

In accordance with the power vested in me as Mayor by the Charter of the City of Austin,I

may 4,1908,and resolu-tion of the Council adopting said report .
The petition , date January,1,1908 ,addressed to the Mayor and members of the City Council
of the City of Austin,requesting the open-ing of fourth street in Hyde Park,Travis
County,Texas,where the same connects Avenue H with Duval street,was filed by certain
Citizens living in the northern portion of the City of Austin,and after its filing
representations were made to the Cityby parties interested in the granting of said
petition to the effect that ,if the City Council would order the street opened in
accordance with said petition,the Citizens interested in the granting of said petition
would pay to the City all expense necessary to the opening thereof .That the petition,the
report of a majority of the Committee ,and the resolution adopting the report of said
Committee,bear no record of these promises ,and there has been up to this date no money
placed at the disposal of the City or any of its officers towards defraying the expenses
incident to the forcible opening of said street by the City .

The City of Austin is now close run and in need of funds with which to care for and work
the streets which have already been thrown open to the public,and has no money with which
to condemn and open new streets .
Therefore,until the parties interested in the opening of Fourth street see fit to give to
the City of Austinthe money necessary to defray the expense of the opening of said
street,I must return the resolution authorizing the City to open said street with my veto
Respectfully submitted
F M Maddox,Mayor .
